metadata.title: Bank of America raises Micron price target to $1,550

content.text:
Bank of America reiterated a Buy rating on Micron Technology on Monday and raised its price target to $1,550 from $1,250, pointing to SanDisk's recent investor day as evidence that the memory chip industry may be entering a more durable, less cyclical phase.
Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya puts Micron's 2030 earnings per share somewhere in the $200-to-$250 range, a trajectory he says works out to a CAGR exceeding 30% measured from fiscal 2026. By contrast, the prevailing Wall Street consensus clusters around $160 to $170 at the cycle peak. Arya argues that consensus estimates underestimate Micron's structural earnings power.
The analysis draws heavily on SanDisk's investor day, held August 13, at which the memory chipmaker projected revenue growth at a mid-to-high-teens percentage rate from fiscal 2028 through 2030, with adjusted gross margins of around 80% over that period. SanDisk also revealed a $93.9 billion customer backlog and announced that eight customers have entered its New Business Model agreements — long-term arrangements that lock in both volumes and pricing terms in advance.
Arya applied a similar framework to Micron, assuming comparable supply discipline, customer commitments, and AI-driven memory demand. "The key debate is whether Micron remains a peak-cycle earnings story or is transitioning toward a structurally higher earnings power model," Arya wrote in a note to clients. "Memory has historically been viewed as the most cyclical segment of semis, but SNDK's Analyst Day suggests the industry may be entering a more durable phase."
Bank of America also named Micron one of its highest-conviction ideas for the second half of the year, according to TipRanks. The $1,550 price target implies roughly 50% upside from current levels.
Micron's revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended May 28, was $41.46 billion, up 346% from the same period a year earlier, and earnings per share were $25.11. Management has noted that the long-term supply contracts Micron has been executing are intended to make its revenue stream more stable and easier to forecast going forward.
The bull case rests on whether tighter supply conditions and structured customer deals represent a lasting shift. If demand outpaces supply constraints or traditional oversupply dynamics return, the longtime boom-and-bust pattern for memory chips could resume.
Thirty Wall Street analysts tracked by TipRanks collectively rate Micron a consensus Strong Buy, with 29 of those recommendations being outright Buys and one a Hold over the past three months. Those same analysts set an average price target of $1,563.39 on the shares.
